input: Immediate children of the configured registrations directory containing qnc-app.json; executable basenames resolve only in the explicitly configured executable directory.
applications: Only enabled, valid registrations with a nonempty regular executable file. On Unix at least one execute permission bit must be set. This is installation presence, not proof of successful startup, ABI compatibility or embedded adapter availability.
unavailable: Diagnostic IDs, labels and reasons: disabled, missing_executable, not_executable. These records are never menu candidates.
ordering: priority_group is a single lowercase letter a-z from each registration. Groups sort alphabetically; label/application_id order variants within a group for display only. Gaps are valid: a-c-d, never a-d-c. Legacy numeric order is not the new workflow priority.
group_semantics: Multiple installed variants may have the same group. Radio/option controls select at most one variant per group; choosing another replaces the previous choice. No selection skips the group. This is per-template exclusivity, never a global reservation. Save validation rejects unavailable IDs, duplicates and two variants in the same group, then orders the selected groups alphabetically. Existing template drafts intersect their saved choices with current availability; absent applications are not displayed and do not block creation. Stored templates are never rewritten by catalog reads.
failure_policy: Malformed manifests, duplicate IDs/tabs, inaccessible inputs or invalid existing output abort publication. Preserve the previous catalog. Empty verified registrations publish an empty catalog. No fallback app names.
replacement_policy: Publish a fully validated temporary JSON file with atomic replacement. Replace only an existing valid catalog with the same catalog URI; never overwrite an unrelated file. Remove missing registrations from the next snapshot.
freshness_policy: One-shot inventory at observed_at_unix_ms, not a live availability service. Run on installation/registration changes and before refreshing the available-app menu. Consumers must not treat a saved inventory as a guarantee that an app still starts.
public_identity_policy: QNC URI and neutral IDs only. Absolute paths and host-specific filesystem separators are private publisher configuration, not catalog fields.
reader_policy: Any application/module may read the catalog. No caller allowlist. Consumers read applications, not unavailable, as available choices.
transport_policy: The publisher runs on the installation host and produces a portable artifact. The independent reader supports resolver-bound local files and read-only HTTP(S) GET via LAN/intranet authority mappings. No remote discovery or HTTP server is implemented here. Network requests are bounded, have a timeout, reject redirects and verify the requested catalog URI.
lifecycle: Read registrations, check executable presence without running them, publish JSON, close and exit. No watcher, scheduler, shell or app process required.
business_boundary: No project settings, active project, workflow status, selected template or media data. The selected application sequence and group snapshot belong to the template/project database and must respect group order and one-per-group selection. Catalog changes never rewrite those databases. The select command is a read-only query/validation, not a template writer.
integration_status: Independent producer and public reader/selection library implemented. Project uses only the reader, never the producer, and stores validated group sequence in its own template/project DB. Shell catalog consumption and automatic navigation remain follow-up steps.
